criteria.description: One normative production-runtime architecture supersedes conflicting active design statements.
criteria.notes: The terminal review found one canonical record and zero open normative conflicts.

criteria.description: Every capability is labeled delivered, retained, amended, proposed, retired, or historical with evidence for delivered claims.
criteria.notes: No proposed production capability is represented as currently shipped.

criteria.description: Python and Phase 1-3 behavior is classified into preserved laws, amendments, retirements, and later proof obligations.
criteria.notes: Frozen Phase 1-3 evidence remains historical and byte-verified.

criteria.description: Every mission-state category has one writable authority and explicit projection rules.
criteria.notes: The review found zero duplicate writable authorities and zero unowned categories.

criteria.description: The architecture distinguishes memory-primary projections, durable acknowledgement evidence, and ephemeral observations.
criteria.notes: Durable success precedes authoritative acknowledgement.

criteria.description: Checkpoint, journal, restore, runtime-epoch, and reconciliation semantics support safe mission resumption.
criteria.notes: WP01 cycle 2 established deterministic bounded checkpoint fallback and degraded/closed behavior.

criteria.description: Playback is deterministic, side-effect-free, versioned, and portable.
criteria.notes: Playback reduces recorded inputs and cannot invoke adapters.

criteria.description: The target production graph is GapDB-only and identifies the mission that must prove SQLite removal.
criteria.notes: SQLite remains historical evidence only; M2 owns structural absence proof.

criteria.description: Beads is the default first-party tracker behind provider-neutral ports and cannot grant execution authority.
criteria.notes: Tracker state and mission authority remain separate.

criteria.description: Orchestrator API 2.0 exposes the governed mission lifecycle through typed capabilities.
criteria.notes: This is a ratified contract, not a claim that the server ships today.

criteria.description: Mutation uses named typed commands and rejects generic transitions, manufactured authority, and direct store or Git mutation.
criteria.notes: The command vocabulary is closed and authority is host-owned.

criteria.description: Native operations define resumable handles, progress, input, cancellation, terminal results, and idempotent replay.
criteria.notes: Operation semantics are transport-independent.

criteria.description: Mission progress reports phase, generation, counts, active work, review and integration position, critical path, blockers, next actions, drift, and revision.
criteria.notes: List, get, and watch are projections of one application model.

criteria.description: CLI, hosted clients, Team Kitty, CI, dashboards, and optional adapters project the same application capabilities.
criteria.notes: No transport owns alternate workflow semantics.

criteria.description: Acceptance claims compose organization, project, mission-type, and mission requirements without assuming a language stack.
criteria.notes: The proposed acceptance kernel is ecosystem-neutral.

criteria.description: Claim-to-provider bindings are explicit and revision-pinned; stack detection is suggestion-only.
criteria.notes: Missing qualified providers produce actionable refusal.

criteria.description: Acceptance evidence binds claim, candidate, generation, policy, provider, runner, time, and artifact digests.
criteria.notes: Published examples validate against the JSON Schema.

criteria.description: The gate defines pass, fail, error, skipped, and waived outcomes with freshness and strict policy union.
criteria.notes: Waivers are explicit evidence and never inferred from provider output.

criteria.description: Qualification is dependency-aware, concurrent, content-reusable, invalidatable, and progress-projectable.
criteria.notes: Reuse keys bind content and policy rather than filenames or timestamps.

criteria.description: MCP is optional, independently packaged, and contributes no unique workflow capability or core dependency.
criteria.notes: Core installation and qualification remain MCP-free.

criteria.description: The optional adapter is pinned to MCP 2026-07-28 stateless semantics and does not treat protocol sessions as authority.
criteria.notes: M7 must pin an immutable Tasks extension revision before implementation.

criteria.description: Negotiated MCP Tasks project native operations without becoming mission, run, lease, decision, cancellation, TTL, or evidence authority.
criteria.notes: Task loss or expiry cannot revoke domain authority.

criteria.description: Dependency and mutant guards prevent adapters from leaking into the authority kernel.
criteria.notes: The architecture guard and rejecting mutants passed.

criteria.description: The implementation program is acyclic and dependency-ordered with bounded missions, contract dependencies, falsification experiments, and gates.
criteria.notes: Schema, unique-ID, maximum-dependency, acyclicity, critical-path, and parity checks passed.

criteria.description: Every proposed mission has explicit entry evidence, exit evidence, non-goals, and go/no-go conditions.
criteria.notes: All M1-M7 program rows are bounded and independently governed.

criteria.description: Active README, project-plan, ADR, contract, and operational guidance is migrated or explicitly retained as history.
criteria.notes: Ten normative conflicts are recorded and closed; historical evidence remains immutable.

criteria.description: M1 is selected as the smallest first mission capable of disproving the most consequential unproven architecture claim.
criteria.notes: M1 owns the GapDB durability, recovery, ambiguity, and replay disproof boundary.

criteria.description: An adversarial review attacks authority, recovery, evidence, API, acceptance, MCP isolation, and program overreach.
criteria.notes: All 32 scenarios pass with zero unresolved blocker/high findings.

criteria.description: All fifteen non-functional requirements are mapped and independently verified.
criteria.notes: Traceability, authority clarity, delivery honesty, boundedness, portability, links, recovery, neutrality, isolation, evidence economy, and independent review all pass.

criteria.description: All eighteen mission constraints are mapped and independently verified.
criteria.notes: The mission remains documentation-only and preserves every locked authority, storage, API, acceptance, MCP, history, and filesystem boundary.

criteria.description: All ten measurable success criteria are mapped to passing evidence.
criteria.notes: The terminal report records exact source, full coverage, ten closed conflicts, and no blocker/high findings.
